title: Golden Gate assembly: GFP into pUC19
summary: Open pUC19 by PCR across 395-451, amplify GFP with BbsI tails, join the 2 fragments in one Golden Gate reaction, and confirm the clone by colony PCR and sequencing.
highlights: One reaction joins 2 fragments: pUC19 backbone (2630 bp) and GFP (717 bp).
GFP reads on the opposite strand from lac promoter, 61 bp away, so that promoter does not transcribe it.
There is no ribosome binding site annotated ahead of GFP, so the clone is not expected to make its protein.
The insertion interrupts lacZα, so correct clones are white and empty vector is blue on X-gal and IPTG.

checks.name: sites
checks.detail: BbsI no longer cuts the product

checks.name: primers
checks.detail: 9 designed, 5 with a warning, 0 failing: GC on 2, GC clamp on 2, Tm on 1; not judged: full-primer Tm, 3' end stability

materials.name: Q5 DNA Polymerase and its reaction buffer
DpnI
materials.note: cuts the methylated plasmid template only

materials.name: PCR and gel cleanup spin columns
LB agar plates with ampicillin or carbenicillin, 80 µg/mL X-gal and 200 µM IPTG
OneTaq Quick-Load 2X Master Mix with Standard Buffer

equipment: Agarose gel rig and power supply
Heat block or water bath at 42 °C
Shaking incubator and a plate incubator at 37 °C

steps.title: Amplify pUC19 backbone
instructions: Thaw the buffer, dNTPs and primers on ice, then vortex and spin them down.
Mix the master mix and put it in each tube, then add the pUC19 template.
Run the program below: 64 °C annealing and 60 s extension for a 2662 bp product.
notes: 20 cycles, which is the fewest NEB finds enough for an amplicon going into an assembly; fewer cycles means fewer PCR errors.
The primers carry a BbsI site pointing back into the part, so cutting the amplicon leaves TGGC and ATGA.
expected: One band at 2662 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the pUC19 template is there.
Raise the annealing temperature, or gel-purify the band of the right size.

steps.title: Amplify GFP
instructions: Thaw the buffer, dNTPs and primers on ice, then vortex and spin them down.
Mix the master mix and put it in each tube, then add the GFP template.
Run the program below: 64 °C annealing and 20 s extension for a 749 bp product.
notes: 20 cycles, which is the fewest NEB finds enough for an amplicon going into an assembly; fewer cycles means fewer PCR errors.
The primers carry a BbsI site pointing back into the part, so cutting the amplicon leaves ATGA and TGGC.
expected: One band at 749 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the GFP template is there.
Raise the annealing temperature, or gel-purify the band of the right size.

steps.title: Check the PCRs on a gel
instructions: Pour a 1% agarose gel.
Load 5 µL of each reaction beside the ladder.
Run until the dye front is two thirds down the gel.
expected: pUC19 backbone: one band at 2662 bp.
GFP: one band at 749 bp.

troubleshooting.problem: A smear or an extra band
troubleshooting.solution: Gel-purify the band of the right size; a wrong template in the assembly gives wrong clones.

steps.title: Digest the plasmid template with DpnI
instructions: Add 20 units of DpnI to the pUC19 backbone PCR and mix.
Incubate at 37 °C for 60 minutes.
notes: DpnI cuts GATC only where Dam has methylated it, so it cuts pUC19 (15 Dam sites) and leaves the PCR product, which carries no methylation.
This step is not in NEB's Golden Gate protocol; the incubation is this package's choice.
expected: Nothing visible. The digest shows up later as fewer colonies carrying the template plasmid.

troubleshooting.problem: Many colonies on the no-insert control
troubleshooting.solution: The template survived: digest longer, or use more DpnI.

steps.title: Purify every amplicon
instructions: Run each reaction over a spin column and elute in the smallest volume the kit allows.
notes: NEB asks for purified amplicons: polymerase carried over from the PCR fills in the four-base overhangs, which blunts the ends and mis-assembles them.
expected: Clean DNA, free of polymerase, primers and dNTPs.

troubleshooting.solution: Elute twice through the same column, or pool two reactions before purifying.

steps.title: Measure every concentration
instructions: Measure each purified amplicon by A260 or with a fluorometer.
Work out the volume that carries the picomoles the next table asks for.
notes: Picomoles, not nanograms: the shorter fragment weighs less at the same molar ratio. Mass to moles here is NEBioCalculator's 36.04 + 615.94 per base pair, which is about 5% off the 650 Da per base pair of NEB's manuals.
expected: pUC19 backbone: 0.05 pmol is 81.98 ng, so 82 ng/µL or more fits in 1 µL.
GFP: 0.05 pmol is 23.07 ng, so 23 ng/µL or more fits in 1 µL.

troubleshooting.problem: Too dilute to fit in the reaction
troubleshooting.solution: Concentrate the amplicon, or scale the reaction up.

steps.title: Set up the Golden Gate reaction
instructions: Thaw the master mix on ice and mix it well; it is viscous.
Pipette the DNA into the tube first, then the rest.
Mix gently and spin down.
notes: The volumes above assume the concentrations measured in the step before; pipette the volume that gives the picomoles, and make the difference up with water.

tables.title: Golden Gate assembly, NEBridge Ligase Master Mix (M1100)

expected: A 15 µL reaction holding every fragment.

troubleshooting.problem: The DNA does not fit the reaction volume
troubleshooting.solution: Concentrate the fragments, or scale the whole reaction up.

steps.title: Run the Golden Gate program
instructions: Put the tube in the thermocycler and run the program below.
notes: Junction positions are 0-based, on the product.
expected: Nothing visible. The 60 °C soak at the end is a digest, not heat inactivation: it cuts vector that never opened or has closed again, so fewer empty colonies grow.
The product carries ATGA at 395, joining pUC19 backbone to GFP.
The product carries TGGC at 1112, joining GFP to pUC19 backbone.

troubleshooting.solution: Keep the 60 °C soak, and check the template was digested with DpnI.
Raise the cycle count, or plate more of the outgrowth.

steps.title: Transform and plate
instructions: Thaw 50 µL of NEB 5-alpha Competent E. coli (C2987) on ice for 10 minutes.
Add 2 µL of the assembly and flick the tube four or five times.
Hold on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat shock at 42 °C for 30 seconds.
Return to ice for 5 minutes.
Add 950 µL of outgrowth medium and shake at 37 °C for 60 minutes at 250 rpm.
Spread 50 µL of a 1:5 dilution on a warmed plate and grow overnight at 37 °C.
cautions: Competent cells die if they warm up; keep them on ice until the shock.
notes: The plate reads colour only with an alpha-complementing host, such as NEB 5-alpha Competent E. coli (C2987). A host that cannot complement gives white colonies whatever the clone carries.
The clone is not expected to make GFP: it reads on the opposite strand from lac promoter and no ribosome binding site is annotated ahead of it.
expected: Hundreds of colonies; NEB counts about 687 correct ones from a single-insert assembly with 2.5 µL of the outgrowth plated.
Correct clones are white and empty vector is blue: the insertion interrupts lacZα, which is then not there to complete the host's own.

troubleshooting.solution: Check the antibiotic and the cells' efficiency, and plate the rest of the outgrowth.
Plate a smaller volume or a greater dilution next time.

steps.title: Screen colonies by PCR
instructions: Touch a well-separated colony with a sterile toothpick and stir it into the tube until the liquid clouds.
Streak the same toothpick onto a numbered plate, so the clone survives the PCR.
Run the program below and load 5 µL on a 2% gel.
notes: The long first step at 94 °C lyses the cells; there is no purified template.

components.name: OneTaq Quick-Load 2X Master Mix with Standard Buffer (M0486)

expected: Each of the 2 junctions is read: the flanking pair crosses them all, and each junction primer stops inside its own insert.
Correct clone: 160 bp, 897 bp.
Empty vector: 236 bp.
Reversed insert: 220 bp, 897 bp.
A reversed insert is told from a correct one, because the two vector primers sit at different distances from their own junctions.

troubleshooting.solution: The colony was too much material: touch a smaller one, or dilute it.

troubleshooting.problem: Every colony reads as empty vector
troubleshooting.solution: The template survived the DpnI digest, or the vector re-closed; check the 60 °C soak ran.

steps.title: Confirm the clone by sequencing
instructions: Miniprep two or three colonies that read as correct.
Send each with both sequencing primers.
Check the read across every junction and the whole of each insert.
notes: NEB asks for the assembly to be confirmed by sequencing across the junctions whatever the screen said.
A provider whose read is shorter than the lengths above needs a further primer inside the inserts.
expected: Sequencing forward anneals 119 bp from its own junction and has to read 836 bp to cover the far one.
Sequencing reverse anneals 113 bp from its own junction and has to read 830 bp to cover the far one.
The junctions read as ATGA and TGGC, and the parts match GFP.

troubleshooting.problem: The read starts too close to the junction
troubleshooting.solution: Move the primer further out; the first bases after a primer are unreadable.
